checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses.
checklist.evidence: Local instance with a unique marker in every secret. 16 public reads gave leaks=0 envname=0 under grep -Eoc; the only 2 hits, on /metrics, were the metric name pulse_api_location_last_result_timestamp_seconds, which matched the API-secret pattern. GET /admin/config shows literal header values and bodies as {"keep":true} and heartbeat checks as hasSecret: true; the export lists 6 withheld values in redacted; token lists and audit entries hold no secret. GET /probe/checks with a probe token serves literal values (documented). Draft, internal and note texts appear only on /admin/manual-incidents; public GET /manual-incidents/2 (internal) and /3 (draft) give 404. 422 answers name the field and the rule, never the value. 19 broken startup files and settings: one line each, exit 2, leaks=0. 3 hostile hot reloads were rejected naming the path and the rule only. Logs: 134 lines, 0 hits for every marker and both API-created token secrets, 0 error-level lines. Test 'security sentinels: every cell of the table of where values may appear' passed. SMTP not applicable (no mail); no upstream requests (item 6).

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes.
checklist.evidence: 78 requests. 9 admin paths: 401 for no token, Basic or an unknown bearer, and 403 for a probe token. 401 comes before 405 (PATCH /admin/checks, POST /admin/config, DELETE /admin/tokens, POST /admin/audit) and before 413 (2 MB on POST /admin/checks: 401 without a token, 403 with a probe token, 413 with the admin token). On /admin/manual-incidents, 405 and a bad-id 404 come before auth, as documented. Write order with the admin token: 400 bad JSON, 428, 400 for If-Match *, 400 id mismatch, 412, 422, 409, 404. A read token gets 200 on config and export, and 403 on tokens and writes; the grant rule gives 403. Feature off: 24 requests got 404 with no log line. Throttle: the 11th failure gives 429 with retry-after: 60, also for a valid token, and X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded are ignored; another client gets 200, and public and probe routes get 200. Heartbeat: identical 401 for a wrong secret, an unknown id and a probe token. A request target the URL parser rejects gives 400 invalid request target before auth (50/50, 0 stderr lines).

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write.
checklist.evidence: Over-limit bodies give 413 with the state unchanged: DELETE /admin/checks/:id (2 MB), private DELETE, publish, draft DELETE and notes POST (20 KB), token revoke and rotate (2 MB), heartbeat ping with the right secret (20 KB), maintenance POST and component PUT (2 MB), legacy resolve (2 MB). Admin GET config, export, tokens, token and both audit routes give 413 with 2 MB. 300 MB chunked streams give 413 within 0.004 s, or 401 without a token, and RSS went from 77,412 to 79,176 KB. A body that holds a whole second request gave responses=1 everywhere (control 2). CL+TE, two CL and a negative CL give 400; a 64 KB header gives 431. Deep nesting gives 400 or 422, never 500. Finding security-api-2026-11-05-1: the legacy DELETE /manual-incidents/:id answers 204 to a 2,000,000-byte body. Note security-api-2026-11-05-2: the private GET routes ignore the body.

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type.
checklist.evidence: Fuzz script, 523 cases (undefined, null, NaN, Infinity, BigInt, Symbol, a function, Date, arrays, a null prototype, __proto__ and constructor keys, deep arrays, a throwing Proxy, a 5 MB string, typed field values, accessors) over validateResult, 11 contract validators, parseConfig, parseCheck, parseTokens, parseAdminTokens and bearerSecret. The contract validators never threw and never ran a getter, and Object.prototype was not polluted. Throws came only from a throwing Proxy and from non-string input to bearerSecret, which neither JSON.parse nor a header can produce (note security-api-2026-11-05-3). HTTP: bad limit, before, since, status and audit keys give 400; a bad note or token id gives 404. Probe: a location mismatch and a heartbeat result give 403; future or old timestamps and bad fields give 400; a __proto__ key changes nothing. Token and incident inputs: strict 400 with the field rule; a __proto__ key on a check, component or window gives 422. Each bad environment setting gives one line and exit 2.

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs.
checklist.evidence: All bodies and files go through JSON.parse (pulse-kit readJsonBody, src/server.ts:404, src/token-routes.ts:88, src/config.ts:474, src/config.ts:530), which makes no accessors (JSON.parse makes accessors? false). validateResult refuses accessor bodies before any read (src/server.ts:157-163), and the fuzz run counted 0 getter runs there and in every contract validator. The file parsers run a getter once only on a direct call with an accessor input, which parsed JSON cannot hold (note security-api-2026-11-05-3).

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers.
checklist.evidence: A search of the non-test sources for fetch(, http(s).request, net.connect, createConnection, dns., lookup(, Bun.connect, WebSocket, x-forwarded, forwarded, headers.host and process.env hits only process.env in src/main.ts:12, src/main.ts:27 and src/backup-main.ts:10. ss -tanp showed only the listener of the API process, so it follows no redirect. Forwarded headers are ignored (throttle test). Env references are never resolved by the API, and names outside PULSE_HEADER_ give 422. gopher: and userinfo URLs give 422. Link-local http and loopback tcp targets are accepted (201); the probe fetches them (note).

Checks file writes use an exclusive temp file (wx), copy mode and owner, fsync, a second revision check, rename and an fsync of the directory (src/config-fs.ts). The mode was kept (644 to 644, and 600 through a symlink). 6 parallel component creates gave 1x201 and 5x412, the file stayed valid JSON, and no .tmp was left. 6 parallel database check creates gave 1x201 and 5x412. A read-only directory gave 503 for a file write, while a database check write gave 201. A symlinked checks file was replaced by a regular file and the target was unchanged (note). Backup: exit 0 with mode 600, exit 2 for an existing target and for a dangling symlink (link target not created), exit 1 for a missing directory, exit 2 for wrong arguments, and no temp directory was left. Paths come only from settings and argv.

checklist.item: Dependencies, Docker base images and CI actions pinned and approved (docs/approved-packages.md).
checklist.evidence: Runtime: zod 4.6.7, pulse-contract #9ab7e24 and pulse-kit #c6d2cba, exact pins with integrity hashes, all approved; the gh compare API gives behind_by=0 against main for contract, kit and config. Dev dependencies match the dev table, and the pulse-config SHA equals both reusable workflow refs. bun audit exited with 1: minimatch@10.2.6 (moderate), reached only through dev eslint; bun audit --prod found no vulnerabilities (exit 0). Both Dockerfile stages and the bench helper use the approved oven/bun:1.4.0-alpine digest, and the final stage runs as bun. actions/checkout v7.0.1, oven-sh/setup-bun v2.2.0 and actions/upload-artifact v7.0.2 are approved pins; every checkout sets persist-credentials: false; pulse-workflows: ok (2 files, 8 uses), exit 0.

findings.title: The legacy DELETE /manual-incidents/:id deletes without enforcing the body limit
findings.command: Bun script against a local instance with the admin token: create a public incident, DELETE /manual-incidents/<id> with a 2,000,000-byte body, then GET it. The same on DELETE /admin/manual-incidents/<id>, a keep-alive check with a whole request in the body, and a legacy resolve with 2 MB.
findings.excerpt:
legacy DELETE 2MB body: 204; GET after: 404
private DELETE 2MB body: 413; GET after: 200
legacy DELETE with a request in its body: responses=1 statuses=204
legacy resolve 2MB body: 413; resolvedAt after: null
findings.impact: The documented 413 for a body over 1,000,000 bytes (docs/rest-api.md:40) and over 16 KiB for manual incidents (docs/rest-api.md:288) fails on this one write route. The delete runs, without any desync. An admin token with incidents is needed.
findings.fixDirection: Read and drop the body with MANUAL_INCIDENT_MAX_BODY_BYTES before store.remove, like skipBody on the private route, and add the route to the test 'oversized bodies across methods cannot reach a write'.

findings.title: The private GET /admin/manual-incidents[/:id] routes answer without reading the body, unlike every other admin GET
findings.command: Limits script with the admin token: GET with a 2 MB body to every admin read route, then a 300 MB chunked GET /admin/manual-incidents.
